extracted.intended_audience: students and emerging creatives submitting to the D&AD New Blood Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit a student/emerging-creative response to one of the real-world briefs for the D&AD New Blood Awards, aiming to meet judging criteria and achieve a Pencil award. The page describes award tiers, the core judging criteria, deadlines and entrant audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good idea
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the three judging criteria explicitly listed by D&AD: 'a good idea.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a required element to hit for Graphite and above; no further elaboration on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well executed
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the three judging criteria explicitly listed by D&AD: 'well executed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a required element to hit for Graphite and above; no further elaboration on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant to the brief
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the three judging criteria explicitly listed by D&AD: 'relevant to the brief.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must answer the real-world briefs issued by the sponsoring brands; relevance to the brief is a core judging dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphite Pencil (meet three judging criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: To snag a Graphite Pencil, you have to hit the three judging criteria – a good idea, well executed, and relevant to the brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphite indicates an entry that satisfies all three core criteria (idea, execution, brief relevance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Yellow Pencil (outstanding work)
rubrics_metrics.description: The D&AD Yellow Pencil is for outstanding work that nails the judging criteria and almost certainly causes a pang of jealousy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents a level above Graphite: not only meets core criteria but stands out as outstanding and highly desirable/impactful.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Pencil (creativity for good / purpose-driven)
rubrics_metrics.description: The D&AD White Pencil is for next-level ideas that harness the power of creativity to do good in the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be awarded for any of the briefs if the work 'weaves in purpose' — i.e., demonstrable social/purpose impact is a decisive criterion for this award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Pencil (best of the best)
rubrics_metrics.description: Yellow and White winners compete for the award that represents the best of the best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Black Pencil is the top award, chosen from among outstanding (Yellow) and purpose-driven (White) winners; it denotes the very highest accolade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wood Pencil (recognised winner tier)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you make it to the D&AD Wood Pencil winners list, then you've fought off some seriously tough competition and are miles ahead of the game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wood Pencil is a recognised winners tier on the D&AD scale. The page does not list specific criteria for Wood beyond being a shortlisted/winner level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to a real brand brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Top brands issue real world briefs; entrants must 'Enter your response to the briefs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are judged on how they respond to the briefs issued by partner brands — answering the brief is a procedural requirement and an evaluative dimension (see 'relevant to the brief').

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrant eligibility: students and emerging creatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The New Blood Awards are described as 'Our awards for students and emerging creatives' and 'discover and showcase the fiercest new talent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The competition is targeted at students and emerging creatives — eligibility and intended audience are a requirement for entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadline to submit your entry to the New Blood Awards: 17 March 2026, 5pm GMT (New Blood Awards Deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission is a procedural requirement for being considered; entries submitted after the deadline will not be eligible.
